newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India up again as Bombay climbs.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India up again as Bombay climbs.

text.p: Indian Global Depositary Receipts posted steady gains on Thursday following a speculative rise in Bombay earlier, traders said.
"We saw some activity from market-makers but not much investor interest," a trader said.
Dealers said the GDR market had been relatively active despite light trade in Bombay due to the absence of Far East funds for the Chinese New Year.
A trader said Reliance and Grasim had attracted interest, with Reliance rising 36 cents to $14.00/$15.00 and Grasim firming 42 cents to $14.37/$15.37.
He said the market was seen hampered in the short term ahead of the Indian budget on February 28, with local market prices likely to trade around current levels until then.
Bombay's benchmark 30-share index was 47.88 at 3,402.60 points following late speculative buying.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed 1.51 points or 2.29 percent up at 67.35, with the premium over the local market at 15.64 percent from 14.16 percent.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended down 0.88 points at 65.92 with a premium of 42.95 percent over the local market.
The Taiwan GDR Index finished a quiet day down 0.88 points at 100.32, with a premium of 3.80 percent to the local market, which was closed for the Lunar New Year.
Accton Technology Corp, which was priced at $7.51 per GDR earlier in the week, was last at $7.65.
